## Diagnose setup

Run `forgecycle doctor`. It checks Git history and identity, JSON structure, model
placeholders, each policy's `decomposer`, `planner`, `builder`, and `reviewer`
candidate lists (known candidates, no duplicates, configured adapters, writable
builders), `git`, adapter binaries, and adapter versions without
making a paid model call. It warns about `instructions` files that exist but
are not committed at HEAD: run worktrees will not contain them, so no agent
sees them.

`forgecycle doctor --ping` goes one step further and makes one real, billed
call per candidate. Every candidate referenced by any policy's `decomposer`,
`planner`, `builder`, or `reviewer` list gets a tiny read-only prompt asking
for the exact reply `FORGECYCLE_PONG`, using its configured adapter, model, and
effort, in the repository root. Each candidate is pinged once even when several
policies or roles use it, and the output lists where it is used:

```text
forgecycle: info: ping agy-low (agy/gemini-3-flash, used by balanced:builder) ok in 4.2s
forgecycle: error: ping codex-high (codex/gpt-5.5, used by balanced:planner, balanced:reviewer) failed: authentication_error (Not logged in)
```

Up to four pings run at once. Each is capped at `--ping-timeout` seconds
(default 120) or the candidate's shorter `timeout_seconds`. Candidates on a
quota cooldown are skipped with a warning. A failed ping exits 65 and names the
candidates; an answer other than `FORGECYCLE_PONG` is only a warning, because
the candidate did respond. Pings are not recorded as candidate invocations in
the operation journal, so `observe --summary` is unaffected. If a ping changes
the repository's Git state, doctor fails.

## Find unfinished task runs

`forgecycle status` shows which task run reserves the repository and lists
every task run that is not done or abandoned. Each line gives the task run
ID, its state, and its stop kind with detail; an active task run whose
process is gone reads `interrupted`. The first next command follows on its own
line, marked `(human decision)` when it needs one:

```text
Reservation: task run 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4
Task runs:
  20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4  blocked  agent_failure (quota_exhausted)
    Next: forgecycle task resume 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4 --builder <candidate-id>
```

It only reads and makes no model call, so it is the first thing to run after a
crash or a killed terminal. `--json` prints the same information as an array
of objects with the keys `kind` (`task_run`), `id`, `state`, `phase`,
`stop_kind`, `stop_detail`, `next`, `next_human`, `holds_reservation`,
`pause_requested` (a live run whose pause has not taken effect yet), and,
for a task run started by a roadmap run, `roadmap_run_id` and
`roadmap_task_id`.

A stopped or interrupted task run keeps the repository reservation, so
`task run` for another task run, and `task resume`, `task approve`,
`task reject`, or `task abandon` of a task run that does not hold it, are
refused with exit 21 and `Repository is reserved by run <task-run-id>`. The
refusal prints how to free the repository on the lines after the error: a
`forgecycle: stop: reserved_by=<task-run-id> status=<state>` line, then
`forgecycle: next:` lines that depend on the task run holding it:

- Stopped or interrupted: its stop kind and detail, the next actions its own
  stop block names, `task abandon <task-run-id>` as a human decision, and
  `roadmap resume` when a roadmap run started it. When the refused command was
  given `--auto-resume`, the suggested `task resume` commands repeat it.
- Advanced by a live process: only `task status <task-run-id>`, naming the
  process (`process=<pid>`); wait for it to stop.
- Done, abandoned, or missing: the reservation is stale, and the only step is
  removing `.forgecycle/active.lock` by hand, as a human decision.

A command that acts on a task run or roadmap run another process is
advancing is refused with exit 21 too, by the run's process lock
(`.process.lock` in its run directory): `Run is already being advanced by
process <pid>`, or `Roadmap run <roadmap-run-id> is already being advanced by
process <pid>`. The lines after the error name the run and the process, then
the status command to watch it with:

```text
forgecycle: stop: task_run=<task-run-id> process=<pid>
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task status <task-run-id>  # process <pid> is advancing it; wait until it stops
```

A roadmap run gets `roadmap_run=` and `forgecycle roadmap status`. A
roadmap run that finds its current task run live adds
`forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>` for after that process stops. A
process lock that names no process (`process=unknown`) never clears by
itself; removing it by hand is a human decision.

## Stop a run with Ctrl-C

Ctrl-C, or SIGTERM (`kill <pid>`, a service manager, or an agent tool's
timeout), stops a running `task run`, `task resume`, `task approve`,
`task reject`, `roadmap run`, or `roadmap resume` cleanly:

- ForgeCycle prints `forgecycle: info: interrupt received; stopping the
  running agent or gate (press Ctrl-C again to exit at once)`.
- A running agent CLI gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds. The task
  run is left `interrupted`, as if its process had been killed, and the
  command prints its stop block with `forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>`.
- A running gate's process group is stopped the same way, its `cleanup`
  runs, and the run stops with `gate_failure (interrupted)`.
- `--auto-resume` never resumes after a signal, and an inline approval
  prompt stops waiting, leaving the run at its gate.
- A roadmap run waits for its child task command to stop, records its
  stop, and starts no other task run. With nothing left to record it stays
  `running` and is reported as interrupted;
  `forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>` continues it.
- The command then ends by the signal, so a shell reports 130 (Ctrl-C) or
  143 (SIGTERM).

Stopping waits for a gate's 10-second grace plus its `cleanup`, or for the
agent's 10-second grace. A second Ctrl-C ends ForgeCycle at once and leaves
whatever is still running, as `kill -9` does. A killed ForgeCycle records
nothing: its run reads as `interrupted`, and a gate it started keeps running
until it finishes. `roadmap decompose`, `roadmap questions`, and
`doctor --ping` stop at the first Ctrl-C.

## Pause after the current turn

`forgecycle pause`, run from another terminal in the same repository, stops
whatever runs there once its current Planner, Builder, or Reviewer turn
ends, gates included, so no work is thrown away. It needs no ID:
it asks the task run that holds the repository reservation, or the running
roadmap run, and returns at once.

```text
$ forgecycle pause
forgecycle: info: Pause requested for task run 20261025T153000Z-expose-the-api-c3d4: it stops after its current building turn (turn 2)
forgecycle: next: forgecycle unpause  # cancel the request while the turn runs, or continue once paused
```

`status` then shows `pause requested` next to the run, and `task status`
or `roadmap status` says so too. When the turn ends, the task run stops
with `paused` and `stop_kind: pause_requested`, prints its stop block, and
the command exits 21. A roadmap run stops with it; when the turn that was
running finished the task run, the roadmap run integrates it and stops
before the next task starts. `--auto-resume` never resumes past a pause.

`forgecycle unpause` removes a request that has not taken effect yet, and
the run carries on. Once the run has paused, it continues it in the
foreground: with `roadmap resume` for a roadmap run's task run, which
resumes that task run first, and with `task resume` otherwise. Options of the
paused command, such as `--builder`, are not stored; give them to `unpause`
again. `task resume` and `roadmap resume` continue a paused run as well.
`pause` with nothing running, and `unpause` with nothing paused, exit 1.

Ctrl-C stops at once; `pause` waits for the turn, which can last as long as
the agent's timeout.

The dashboard's notification history (`forgecycle serve`) keeps every past
stop and the command that resolved it. A killed command cannot record its
own stop, so an `interrupted` task run enters the history when the next
command takes it (usually `task resume` or `task abandon`), marked as
detected later.

## Reading a stop

Every stop prints a stop block after its info line, and `forgecycle task status
<task-run-id>` shows the same report later as `Key: value` lines:

```text
forgecycle: info: Run blocked: all candidates failed: builder: quota_exhausted (...)
forgecycle: stop: status=blocked kind=agent_failure detail=quota_exhausted exit=20
forgecycle: stop: resumes into building (turn 4); feedback is read by Builder
forgecycle: stop: inspect .forgecycle/task-runs/<task-run-id>/003-reviewer-review.md
forgecycle: stop: inspect .forgecycle/task-runs/<task-run-id>/events.log
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume <task-run-id> --builder <candidate-id>  # continue building with a candidate that is not on a quota cooldown (forgecycle doctor lists them)
forgecycle: next: forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>  # after the provider quota resets
```

The block adds a `reason:` line when the info line did not already include
the reason. It lists the latest handoff, `events.log`, and the newest
non-empty evidence directory to inspect. A `next (human decision):` line is a
step only a person should take. `task status` also shows `Unaccepted head` when a
Builder commit awaits a handoff-only turn.

`state.json` records the classification as `stop_kind`, with an optional
`stop_detail`. Key tooling off these fields, not `reason`:

| `stop_kind` (`stop_detail`) | Meaning | Next action | Human decision? | `--auto-resume` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `approval_gate` (`after_planning`, `final`, `after_building`, `after_reviewing`) | The approval policy is waiting | `task approve`; at the plan and final gates also `task reject <task-run-id> FEEDBACK.md` | Yes | No |
| `needs_human` | A plan or review asks for direction | `task resume --feedback` answering the latest handoff | Yes | No |
| `technical_block` | A review verdict is `blocked` | Remove the cause named in the findings, then `task resume --feedback` | Yes | No |
| `no_progress` | Three reviews kept the same open findings | `task resume --feedback` with direction, or `task abandon` | Yes | No |
| `agent_failure` (`quota_exhausted`, `rate_limited`) | Every candidate hit a provider limit | `task resume <task-run-id>` with `--planner`, `--builder`, or `--reviewer <candidate-id>` (the role that acts next), or `task resume` after the reset | No | No |
| `agent_failure` (`authentication_error`) | A provider CLI is not logged in | `doctor`; `task resume` after a person logs in, or `task resume` with the next role's flag and a candidate on another adapter | Logging in is | No |
| `agent_failure` (`protocol_error`) | Handoffs stayed invalid after repair | `task resume`, or `task resume` with the next role's flag; `validation_field=` in `events.log` names the field | No | Yes |
| `agent_failure` (`timeout`, `unavailable`, `invocation_error`, `mixed`, `unknown`) | Candidates failed to run or answer | `doctor`, then `task resume`, with the next role's flag to switch candidates | No | Yes |
| `agent_failure` (`config_error`) | The policy or a candidate is not configured | `doctor`, fix `.forgecycle/config.json`, `task resume` | No | No |
| `agent_failure` (`interrupted`) | The turn was canceled | `task resume` | No | Yes |
| `agent_failure` (`worktree_mutated`) | A failed Builder left changes that cannot be kept | Inspect `git -C <worktree> status`; `task resume` once it is committed or restored | Yes | No |
| `unaccepted_head` | A Builder commit's handoff failed validation | `task resume`; Builder re-emits the handoff (see below) | No | Yes |
| `read_only_mutation` | A Planner or Reviewer turn changed the repository | Inspect the worktree, restore it, `task resume` | Yes | No |
| `builder_invariant` | A Builder handoff broke the commit, cleanliness, or test rules | `task resume --feedback` restating the violated rule, or `task resume --builder <candidate-id>` | No | No |
| `review_invariant` | A review broke the revision, findings, test, or clean-worktree rules | `task resume`, or `task resume --reviewer <candidate-id>` | No | Yes |
| `gate_failure` (`interrupted`) | A gate was stopped before it finished | `task resume`; the gate runs again, and finished gates for the same HEAD are reused | No | Yes |
| `gate_failure` (`start_failed`) | A gate could not start, or the worktree HEAD was unknown | `doctor`, fix `review.gates`, `task resume` | Yes | No |
| `gate_failure` (`worktree_mutated`) | A gate changed tracked or untracked files; its result was not stored | Inspect `git -C <worktree> status`, restore it, fix the gate command, `task resume` | Yes | No |
| `pause_requested` | `forgecycle pause` stopped the run between two turns | `forgecycle unpause`, or `task resume` | Yes | No |
| `interrupted` (reported, never stored) | An active state with no live process: the command was killed, or Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stopped an agent turn | `task resume`, with the next role's flag to replace a candidate that was too slow | No | No |
| `unknown` (reported, never stored) | A stopped run with no recorded kind, such as a hand-edited `state.json` | Read `reason` and `resume_state`, then decide | Yes | No |

"No" in the human-decision column means the step is operational: it changes
neither scope nor product decisions, so an operating agent may take it within
the user's cost authorization. "Yes" in the `--auto-resume` column marks the
stops ForgeCycle resumes itself when the invocation passed `--auto-resume`
(see below); without it, ForgeCycle never retries a stopped task run.

## Automatic resume

`forgecycle task run … --auto-resume` and `forgecycle task resume …
--auto-resume` let a task run resume itself, in the same process, after a stop
whose recovery is a plain `task resume` with no input, decision, or wait. The eligible stops are the rows marked in the table above:
`unaccepted_head`, `review_invariant`, `gate_failure` (`interrupted`), and
`agent_failure` with `timeout`, `unavailable`, `invocation_error`,
`protocol_error`, `mixed`, `unknown`, or `interrupted`. Quota and rate limits
are not eligible: the reset can be days away, and the phase has already tried
every candidate in its list, so choosing between another candidate and waiting
belongs to the operator. The flag is off by default because every automatic
resume is a billed model call, and it applies to that invocation only;
`--planner`, `--builder`, and `--reviewer` still apply to the resumed turns.

**Progress rule.** At most one automatic resume is allowed between two
accepted handoffs. `state.json` records `auto_resume_turn`, the turn at the
last automatic resume, and `auto_resumes`, the count over the task run's
life. A stop that comes back with no handoff accepted since then stands, which
covers the same stop recurring and different eligible stops alternating (a
timeout, then a review invariant, then a timeout again). A handoff that ends
in a `review_invariant` or `builder_invariant` stop is stored and counted in
`turn`, but it is not accepted, so it is not progress. Human feedback is a new
turn and counts as progress.

The stop's own block prints as usual, followed by the automatic resume:

```text
forgecycle: stop: status=blocked kind=unaccepted_head exit=20
...
forgecycle: info: auto-resume: unaccepted_head; resuming into building (turn 2)
forgecycle: info: resuming into building (turn 2)
```

When the stop that remains follows an automatic resume with no accepted
handoff since, its block adds `forgecycle: stop: auto_resume=used turn=<n>` and
`task status` prints `Auto-resume: used at turn <n>; no accepted handoff
since`. The plain resume has then already been tried: switch the next role's
candidate with `--planner`, `--builder`, or `--reviewer`, or escalate instead of resuming again. Each automatic resume is also recorded in
`events.log` (`candidate=- outcome=auto_resume … detail=<stop-kind> turn=<n>`)
and in the journal (`state_changed`, `auto-resume after <stop-kind>`). The
command exits with the final stop's code.

## Continue a waiting run

Use `forgecycle task status <task-run-id>` to read the stop report, or `--json` for
the raw state document.

- Approval gate: `forgecycle task approve <task-run-id>`
- Reject with direction: `forgecycle task reject <task-run-id> feedback.md`
- Blocked or needs-human: `forgecycle task resume <task-run-id> --feedback feedback.md`
- Interrupted process: `forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>` (feedback is optional)
- Retry with a different candidate: `forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>
  --planner ID`, `--builder ID`, or `--reviewer ID` replaces that role's
  candidates. Use the role that acts next; the stop
  block's `Next:` line names it. Each lasts for that invocation only,
  and `selected_candidates` records the candidate only when it produces the
  turn's handoff.

Every stop records the phase it stopped in as `resume_state`.
Builder failures resume into `building`, and review failures, no-progress
cycles and `blocked` or `needs_human` verdicts resume into `reviewing`. After
you repair adapter wiring or provider access, `task resume` retries that phase with
its configured candidates. A run blocked on a Builder invocation retries the
Builder turn rather than re-reviewing work that was never built. `task resume`
prints its target and who reads your feedback:

```text
forgecycle: info: resuming into building (turn 4); feedback 003-human-feedback.md will be read by Builder
```

An interrupted task run has no `resume_state`: its process was killed, so no
stop was recorded. It re-enters the phase it was in when that phase is
`planning`, and `reviewing` otherwise, so Reviewer reconciles an interrupted
Builder turn, and replacing the candidate after a killed Builder turn takes
`--reviewer`. `task status`, `task resume`, and the dashboard's task run overview name
the same target. `reason`, `stop_kind`, and
`stop_detail` describe the current stop only: they are cleared when `task resume`, `task approve`, or `task reject`
leaves the stopped state, and at `done`.

Human feedback becomes a new immutable numbered artifact, read by the role
whose turn comes next. An interrupted Builder worktree is reconciled by Reviewer
rather than automatically committed or reverted.

`finding_history` in `state.json` is not a log of findings. It holds one
fingerprint per `changes_requested` review since findings last progressed: the
review's open finding IDs, sorted and joined with commas. Three identical
trailing fingerprints block the run as a no-progress cycle. The list resets
whenever a review newly resolves or supersedes a finding.

### Handoff-only recovery

A Builder may commit cleanly exactly once and still produce a handoff that
fails validation and repair. ForgeCycle keeps that commit as `unaccepted_head`
and blocks with `resume_state: building`. On `task resume`, the Builder
sees `UNACCEPTED_HEAD` in its manifest. It may re-emit the handoff without a
new commit, or add exactly one follow-up commit if your feedback requires
changes. Two or more extra commits fail the commit invariant. A dirty worktree
is never recorded this way; it blocks as before.

### Provider quotas

A candidate whose provider reports an exhausted usage quota (weekly or monthly
limits, plan caps) is classified `quota_exhausted`. It is not retried, and it
is skipped by later turns and runs in the repository until the reset time the
provider reported, or for `quota_cooldown_seconds` (default one hour).
Cooldowns live in `.forgecycle/adapter-cooldowns.json`. `forgecycle doctor`
and the dashboard list the active ones. Delete an entry, or the whole file, to
retry a candidate early.

## Protocol violations

A malformed handoff receives one repair-only call with the same candidate. If it
still fails, ForgeCycle tries the next candidate. Before validation, ForgeCycle
removes recognizable serialization defects (preambles, glued or missing
delimiters, full-width key colons) and fills the facts it owns. Required-test
command drift is repaired within the turn instead of failing the run. Planner
or Reviewer mutation, unexplained human mutation, or invalid commit shape pauses or fails
without destroying data.

Planner and Reviewer turns may create Git-ignored files, such as build output
from running tests. These are not treated as mutations. However, a failed or
paused Planner or Reviewer turn lists any new ignored paths in its `reason`, so whoever resumes can see
the side effects. The journal also records them as `new_ignored_files`
diagnostics.

A turn ends with the agent's final message, and nothing resumes it. On Linux
and macOS, ForgeCycle stops every process a turn started and left running in
the worktree or in the task-run directory, which holds the turn's
`EVIDENCE_DIR`, such as a test suite sent to the background or a browser
daemon: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds. It
prints a warning naming each one and the directory it was in. Processes that
were already running there before the turn, and shells on another terminal,
are left alone. A job started anywhere else, such as `/tmp`, is not found. A Builder that waited for such a process
usually ends without a commit and stops with `builder_invariant`; its work is
still uncommitted in the worktree for the next Builder turn.

## Roadmap run stops

A roadmap run stops at the first task run stop that remains, and never
resolves it: recover the task run with `task` commands, then run
`forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>`. Its stop block follows the
task run's own block, which the child printed:

```text
forgecycle: stop: roadmap_run=<roadmap-run-id> task=FC02 task_run=<task-run-id> kind=task_run_stopped detail=needs_human exit=21
forgecycle: next: forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>  # after task run <task-run-id> is done or abandoned; an abandoned task restarts with a new task run
```

`forgecycle roadmap status <roadmap-run-id>` shows the same stop later, with
every task's status and task runs; `forgecycle status` lists it next to its
task run. A task run that belongs to a roadmap run, recovered with task
commands outside the roadmap run, adds `forgecycle: next: forgecycle roadmap
resume <roadmap-run-id>` to its own stop block and done message, so whoever
recovers it is told to continue the roadmap run.

Feedback that answers a `needs_human` stop of a roadmap run's task run is also
appended to the roadmap run's `decisions.md` as an `H` decision, and
`task resume` prints `recorded the answer as decision H01 of roadmap run …`.
Every task run the roadmap run starts later receives it as part of
`ROADMAP_DECISIONS`, so write the answer to stand on its own. Most such stops
are avoided by answering the roadmap's decisions before `roadmap run`.

| `stop_kind` (`stop_detail`) | Meaning | Next action | Exit | Human decision? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task_run_stopped` (the task run's stop kind) | The current task's task run stopped | Recover the task run with `task resume`, `task approve`, `task reject`, or `task abandon` (its own stop block says which), then `roadmap resume` | 20, 21, or 22, mirroring the task run | As the task run's stop |
| `task_run_stopped` (`interrupted`) | A task run stayed interrupted after `roadmap resume` resumed it once | Read its output; `task resume`, then `roadmap resume` | the `task resume` child's | No |
| `task_run_start_failed` (the child's exit code) | `task run` exited without creating a task run, for example invalid configuration (65) or another task run holding the reservation (21) | Fix the error the child printed, then `roadmap resume`; the task starts again on the integration head | the child's | No |
| `pause_requested` | `forgecycle pause` paused the current task run, or stopped the roadmap run before its next task run | `forgecycle unpause`, or `roadmap resume`, which resumes a task run that paused on request | 21 | Yes |
| `integration_blocked` (`checked_out`) | The integration branch is checked out in a worktree | `git worktree list`, check out another branch there, then `roadmap resume` | 21 | Yes |
| `integration_blocked` (`moved`) | Something other than the roadmap run moved the integration branch | Inspect it; restore it to the recorded `integration_head` and `roadmap resume`, or `roadmap abandon` | 22 | Yes |
| `integration_blocked` (`not_descendant`) | The task run's head is not a fast-forward of the integration head, or it started on another base | `task abandon <task-run-id>`, then `roadmap resume` restarts the task on the integration head | 22 | Yes |

`roadmap resume` also continues a roadmap run that was killed (`running` with
no live process, reported as interrupted): it integrates a task run that
finished in the meantime, adopts a task run it started but did not record,
and continues an interrupted task run, or one that paused on request, with
`task resume`. It refuses with
exit 21 while another process advances the roadmap run or the current task
run. In an attached terminal a child task run asks for approval inline and
the roadmap run continues; detached, a gate stops it with exit 21 until
`task approve <task-run-id>` and `roadmap resume`.

`roadmap abandon <roadmap-run-id>` stops only the roadmap run; its
integration branch and task runs are kept, and a stopped task run keeps the
repository reservation until `task abandon` releases it. To skip a stuck
task, abandon the roadmap run, abandon the stuck task run, and start a new
roadmap run on the integration branch:

```bash
forgecycle roadmap abandon <roadmap-run-id>
forgecycle task abandon <task-run-id>
forgecycle roadmap run <manifest> --base forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id> --skip <done IDs>,<stuck ID>
```

## Stop and clean up

`forgecycle task abandon <task-run-id>` marks a run terminal and releases the repository
reservation while preserving its branch, worktree, and artifacts.

`forgecycle task clean <task-run-id>` accepts only terminal runs and removes only a clean
worktree. It preserves the branch and run artifacts. Dirty worktrees must be
resolved manually; ForgeCycle never resets them.

`forgecycle prune [--worktrees] [--runs] [--force]` clears everything at
once: `--worktrees` deletes the contents of `.forgecycle/worktrees`, `--runs`
deletes the contents of `.forgecycle/task-runs` and `.forgecycle/roadmap-runs`,
and with neither option both are deleted. A roadmap run leaves one worktree
per task, so `prune --worktrees` after it finishes reclaims the space. It lists each directory with its entry count and size (the apparent
size of its files, symbolic links not followed, in binary units such as
`MiB`), prints the total, and asks for confirmation (`[y/N]`);
`--force` skips the prompt, and declining or closed input exits 1 without
deleting anything. Unlike `task clean`, it also removes dirty worktrees, so
uncommitted changes in them are lost; committed work survives on the run
branches, which are kept, as are roadmap runs' integration branches. It
refuses with exit 21 while a task run holds the repository reservation, and
`--runs` refuses while a roadmap run is `running` or `stopped`, naming it,
because the roadmap run depends on its task run directories; abandon them
first. The operation journal behind
`serve` and `observe` lives under the Git common directory and is not touched.

## Source branch changes

A run stays pinned to its recorded base commit. If the original branch advances,
ForgeCycle records the source head at startup, compares it again at completion,
and reports the change in `result.md`. A roadmap run's `result.md` reports it
the same way for the whole roadmap run. Rebasing or merging remains an
explicit user action after completion; for a roadmap run that is
`git merge --ff-only forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id>`.

If a task run stops because the current configuration is invalid or its selected policy was removed, repair `.forgecycle/config.json` (and any global or local override), then run `forgecycle task resume <task-run-id>`. To choose another candidate with a role flag, first list that candidate under the corresponding role in the task run's selected policy.
